ai.description: Minervarya chilapata is a small frog (22–27 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It is distinguished by a prominent, white mid-dorsal stripe and a smooth, unspotted white belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya chilapata* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous glandular fold along the dorsolateral region, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya chilapata* inhabits the floor of subtropical moist deciduous forests and grassy clearings in the Himalayan foothills, typically at elevations below 200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chilapata rainpool frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its hiding spots after dark to forage for small invertebrates near ephemeral forest pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya chilapata* breeds during the monsoon season (June–August). Females lay approximately 200–300 eggs in small, gelatinous clutches within shallow rain pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya chilapata* is endemic to the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas in West Bengal, India, specifically inhabiting the Chilapata Forest at low elevations.
ai.callDescription: The *Minervarya chilapata* produces a high-pitched, rhythmic "chuck-chuck" call, typically heard from shallow rain-filled pools and marshy grasslands during the monsoon.
